title: UV Index Scale
claims: The UV Index scale used in the United States conforms with international guidelines for UV Index reporting established by the World Health Organization.
UV Index 1–2 (Low): no protection needed; minimal sun protection is sufficient.

UV Index 3–7 (Moderate to High): protection needed; seek shade during late morning through mid-afternoon, and use broad-spectrum SPF-15 or higher sunscreen, protective clothing, a wide-brimmed hat and sunglasses.
UV Index 8 or higher (Very High to Extreme): extra protection needed; be careful outside, especially during late morning through mid-afternoon.
Shadow rule: if your shadow is taller than you, UV exposure is likely lower; if your shadow is shorter than you, UV exposure is higher and you should seek shade and protect skin and eyes.
